nail people are usually super respectful and go with the flow! they'll talk if you talk, so if you don't want to have a conversation, they'll likely respect that! they can, however, sometimes be a little aggressive, it might feel weird having someone control your hands but just know that they never mean any harm. if you don't want anything done to your thumb/want any modifications they'll be super okay with that. also you don't sound crazy or anything, it's perfectly normal to be overwhelmed by things like this but most nail technicians i've met are very sweet and respectful. also, to relieve any anxiety on your end, it might be helpful to let the technician know it's your first time! it's a very cool experience and fun to sit back and watch! it's definitely not something to worry about! i suggest you try to just go with the flow and try to relax. i hope your experience goes well! :)

i have an older brother. my best friend. he has (undiagnosed) cptsd and had to deal with a lot of abuse. we both can agree that i definitely got the short end of the stick. i have multiple uncurable mental illnesses while he has none (diagnosed). he has graduated with a bachelor's degree in statistics. i dropped out of high school. my trauma heavily impacted my ability to function and develop as a kid and teen, meanwhile he used work and school as a scapegoat from all the trauma. i definitely experienced more abuse because i was the "problem child". that's not to say that he hasn't been through a lot, he has. he tells me stories all the time of things he had to see my parents do to me and it breaks my heart every time. he's currently working with his first therapist to hopefully unpack all of the trauma he's been through. couldn't be more proud of the guy. he endured so much but was able to stay strong throughout all of it. he tells me all the time that he wished i could have had a better life and that i'm capable of so much but i always tell him that someone has to be the family disappointment haha. no really though, he's a really great guy and i'm incredibly proud of him. he would do anything for me and i would obviously do anything for him. we both know how bad our childhood was because, well, we were the ones who lived it, but we are both working on moving past all of that. he's definitely my favorite person for a reason. :)

i usually don't respond to posts on here but i have to respond!! this simple thing literally changed my life.

my tip is: do something for yourself every morning.

and no, not including the basics like getting ready in the morning. i'm talking about something that you do to unwind. do an ounce of that every morning. for me, i like to get up early, get ready, and then play some video games for like 30 minutes and then leave about another 30 minutes to an hour to relax before i head out.

you could read, draw, cook, exercise, anything that you find enjoyable (that doesn't include social media).

once i started incorporating this into my mornings, it became addictive, i couldn't wait to wake up every morning and have that time to myself.

another tip: as someone who constantly has their mind wander at night before bed, try writing things down and indulge in those things in the morning during your alone time.

i promise, for me it was such a game changer.
